lines.text: You're sprinting across the soccer pitch, kicking the ball, and dripping wet!
Why does your body pump salty water out of your forehead when you run fast?
Your muscles act like car engines; when they work hard, they burn energy and create heat!
You have over three million microscopic sweat glands all across your skin!
Your brain signals these glands to release a thin layer of ninety-nine percent water!
Here comes the genius physics trick: evaporative cooling!
As the outdoor breeze blows across your skin, water transforms into vapor!
It steals heat energy directly off your skin, keeping your body safe from overheating!
Stay hydrated and curious—subscribe to BabyBeats Rhymo!
